note: MSRP excludes destination. No model-year pricing releases could be located on media.ford.com (Ford publishes F-150 pricing through its configurator/order guides rather than press releases), so every year uses the cars.com research trims page ('Starting MSRP' per cab/drive/box configuration, which reflects the latest in-year price) as the row source, with launch-time prices and destination charges from dated secondary articles recorded in notes where they were fetched. Rows per year: each trim in its cheapest listed configuration, plus a second XLT row for SuperCrew 4x4 5.5' box (the common used configuration); the SuperCrew 4x4 price for every other trim is in that row's note. cars.com writes 'LARIAT'; recorded as 'Lariat'. F-150 Lightning (EV) is a separate model line and is not priced here; Raptor R (2023+) and Platinum Plus (2025+) are not listed by cars.com.

gaps: No manufacturer (media.ford.com) pricing source for any year 2016-2026: four site:media.ford.com searches and the media.ford.com F-150 product page returned no pricing release links. All 11 years are secondary (cars.com).

Destination charge not stated by any fetched source for 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020 and 2023 (null; the 2023 Automotive Fleet report of Ford's release says prices exclude destination but gives no gas-truck amount). 2021 ($1,695), 2022 ($1,695), 2024 ($1,995), 2025 ($1,995) and 2026 ($2,795) come from Motor1/Yahoo-Autoblog/Carscoops/Ford Authority/cars.com articles, not from the cars.com trims pages.

2018: launch reports quote XL Regular Cab $28,675 'including destination' (+$270 vs 2017's $27,110 = $27,380 base), while cars.com shows $27,705, so the cars.com figure appears to include a mid-year increase; the implied destination (about $1,295) is an inference and was not recorded.
2021-2025: launch prices differ from the cars.com figures by $50-$2,280 for most trims (mid-year increases); both are recorded (cars.com in msrp, launch in note).
2024 and 2025 STX: cars.com's SuperCab 4x2 price is $2,100-$3,000 above the Carscoops/Motor1/Ford Authority figures; unresolved.

2025: cars.com lists the XL Regular Cab 8' box ($37,450) below the 6.5' box ($38,810); Motor1's launch note ('2WD single-cab 8.0-foot box' $39,345 incl. destination) supports the 8' box being the base configuration.

2026: King Ranch and Platinum are priced below 2025 because RWD became standard (cars.com article, Feb 2026); the 2022 early-year article's figures are internally inconsistent about destination, so its launch prices are flagged as ambiguous in the row notes.
F-150 Lightning: not on any fetched page; not priced.
